# Portable archive TS oracle

Fixed baseline OpenBMB/PilotDeck cc7c4e653b15c8b2cec7bcf2d15d41d69396ae85, Node v22.22.0, ICU 78.2, Darwin arm64. `oracle.json` is normalized from real `createLocalGateway` calls: restore/export, active busy, invalid archive, conflict, missing, compact export, plus saved restore records and model resume messages. UUID, timestamps and temporary project path are intentionally omitted only in normalized summaries; the raw evidence remains in the private run directory. The `compact_projection` entry in `cases` is a direct replay probe; the separate `compact.value` is an actual Gateway export after seeding durable JSONL.

Reproduce on an isolated machine with the fixed baseline and its installed tsx loader: `PDRS_BASELINE=/path/to/PilotDeck node --import /path/to/PilotDeck/node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs capture.mts` (also `compact.mts`, `resume.mts`). The scripts create private temporary homes and project data; no provider calls leave the host. UUIDs, timestamps, project paths and model context diagnostics vary, so compare the listed semantic fields, not raw bytes. Capture writes raw stdout/stderr to caller-selected fresh files.

`native-resume.py` reuses the existing native-history process harness by checking an exact insertion anchor. Invoke with the same `--pilotdeck`, `--control`, `--gateway`, `--sidecar`, `--out` arguments; it snapshots binaries, uses a loopback fake provider, restores the oracle archive through public control, checks durable history/title, streams a real resumed turn, and verifies the provider received hello/world/followup in order. It runs the original native-history checks afterward, with their existing SID/identity cleanup. Execute only against an isolated host with all four binaries built from the verified integrated source. It is a proposed probe until its result, original logs and binary hashes are recorded.

## Incremental nontext/boundary evidence (2026-11-10)

`nontext.mts` drives the actual fixed TS public Gateway. It restores seed sessions, appends canonical durable accepted_input entries, then exports through `exportSessionTranscript`; no private TS helper is substituted for the public entry. Four projection groups cover tool_call object/string/null/undefined/array, empty/mixed tool_result with inner URL/base64 images and PDF pages3/0/-2, tool_result_reference, outer image/PDF/audio/thinking and synthetic/empty text. `oracle.json.nontext.projections` includes input durable entries and actual public outputs, and Rust compares each complete archive. The original candidate oracle sections are preserved.

Twelve restore recipes exercise empty/null title,512/513 UTF16 title units, error precedence(count before title before role),10000/10001 messages and exact2MiB/+1 UTF8 bytes with ASCII/CJK. This confirms fixed TS Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(value),utf8), not UTF16 code-unit size. Empty title is accepted. Rust reconstructs each recipe and compares success or exact errorcode/message. A bounded JSON-size counter replaces the extra full serialized string and checks Unicode escapes/nonfinite/undefined values against the existing codec; validation runs inside owned blocking IO before touching target paths.

The current `nontext` is the unmodified raw capture from the source-built pinned Node22.22.0/ICU78.2/libuv1.52.1 on Linux arm64. Evidence is `_tmp/20261110-gateway-integration/node-pinned-oracle/`: `pinned.json`, `comparison.json`, runtime identity and the existing Node/ICU/libuv source-build chain. All four public projection outputs and twelve validation observations match the earlier mbp2 ICU77.1 run; timestamps in original transcript entries remain the actual new capture times. The full earlier oracle is retained as `original-icu77-oracle.json`; top-level restore/resume/compact sections keep their original provenance. This removes the runtime-version gap for these samples, not the remaining formal Gateway acceptance obligations. Reproduce with the same invocation as capture.mts, substituting nontext.mts and fresh stdout/stderr files.

The native wire suite explicitly pairs all13 original capture case names. Its finished_export unit verifies post-admission archive wire behavior using a restored finished archive; real model completion/resume remains the separate native-resume process probe. Cold archive callers now pass the resolved project explicitly into owner reservation. A blocking-barrier test proves close_project(selected) waits actual cold IO without a cached record/project scope, rejects further cold archive admission while paused, and leaves other projects independent.
